briefs.headline: Chelsea captain Reece James has minor knee surgery
briefs.summary: The club said Friday the right-back was hurt in training and missed the Brentford and Bournemouth matches; no return date was given. James has not played since Sept. 12. Chelsea visit Everton on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Iraola backs Nyoni for a first Premier League start
briefs.summary: With Ryan Gravenberch suspended and Dominik Szoboszlai nursing a hamstring injury, the 19-year-old is likely to partner Alexis Mac Allister at Brentford on Saturday after playing 85 minutes against LASK.

briefs.headline: Ravens likely to start Huntley at Cleveland as Jackson heals
briefs.summary: Tyler Huntley is expected to make a second straight start Sunday with Lamar Jackson's ankle still recovering, AP reported Thursday; Todd Monken faces the team he served as offensive coordinator for three seasons.

briefs.headline: Reds sign utility man Oswaldo Cabrera for $1 million
briefs.summary: The one-year deal agreed Thursday carries up to $200,000 in plate-appearance bonuses. Cincinnati claimed the 27-year-old off waivers from the Yankees on Sept. 18; he went four for 13 as a Red.

briefs.headline: NBA general managers pick the Spurs to win the 2027 title
briefs.summary: San Antonio drew 50% of title votes in the annual survey released Thursday, narrowly ahead of Oklahoma City; Victor Wembanyama took 77% of MVP votes and Dylan Harper was picked for a breakthrough season.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat Dodgers 6-4 to sweep NLCS and reach World Series
briefs.summary: Garrett Mitchell's sixth-inning homer off Tanner Scott capped a rally from a four-run deficit Thursday in Los Angeles; Milwaukee, in its first World Series since 1982, hosts Game 1 Oct. 23 on Fox.

briefs.headline: Halpin homer lifts Guardians past Rays 3-2 for ALCS lead
briefs.summary: The rookie's two-run shot off Griffin Jax in the fifth gave Cleveland a two-games-to-one lead Thursday; Tampa Bay struck out 13 times. Game 4 is tonight at 8 p.m. ET on TBS in Cleveland.

briefs.headline: Miguel Rojas retires after Dodgers' title run ends in a sweep
briefs.summary: The infielder told teammates in the clubhouse Thursday night, still in uniform; Dave Roberts said, "We got outplayed in all facets." Shohei Ohtani's three-run homer had ended a 25-game drought.

briefs.headline: Broncos beat Seahawks 17-14 in overtime on Lutz's 53-yarder
briefs.summary: Ja'Quan McMillian's interception of Sam Darnold set up the kick with 4:53 left in overtime Thursday in Denver; the Broncos sacked Darnold five times while their offense gained 168 net yards.

briefs.headline: College Football Playoff nears a 24-team format for 2027
briefs.summary: ESPN reported Thursday, citing sources, that the deal would drop Power 4 title games and start the season a week earlier; the CFP said only that talks with ESPN continued "constructive."

briefs.headline: Southern Nazarene safety Tyler Ulrich dies after game injury
briefs.summary: The Division II school in Bethany, Okla., said Thursday the 21-year-old sophomore died five days after a "traumatic injury" against Ouachita Baptist; Saturday's game at Southwestern Oklahoma State is canceled.

briefs.headline: Stone scores three in the third as Golden Knights beat Flames 6-2
briefs.summary: Mark Stone's fourth career hat trick came Thursday in Las Vegas; Jack Eichel had a goal and two assists. Vegas leads the NHL with 14 points, and Calgary has one win in seven games.

briefs.headline: Power scores in overtime as Sabres rally past Maple Leafs 5-4
briefs.summary: Buffalo erased a two-goal third-period deficit Thursday in Toronto, with Owen Power scoring at 3:14 of overtime; Kirill Marchenko's hat trick for the Leafs came in his 300th NHL game.

briefs.headline: Former Shotenro takes the Izutsu elder name, JSA says
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association said Friday the Mongolian-born former maegashira (top-division wrestler), 44, now holds the toshiyori (elder) name Izutsu. The Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 23 days out.

prime.item: Day 2. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:54 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, from public bottom; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. The division's proclamations index, read this morning at 5:52 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15, the only October proclamation on its first page; NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:49 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, and the proclamation is the later document. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:49 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 15 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-16T05:43:36-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. The Williams River is coming down off Thursday morning's crest: 950 cfs and 3.71 feet at 5:15 a.m., the last point on the USGS 03186500 two-day trace pulled at 5:48 a.m., against 2,040 cfs and 5.09 feet at 5:15 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark and Thursday's edition reading, so the river is down 1,090 cfs and 1.38 feet on the day and the fetcher's rising flags are WRONG on the day. Its comparison points are not 24-hour marks: the 446 cfs and 2.79 feet in its 24h_ago fields are the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading, 47.5 hours before the current one, the same window-start bug as the last five mornings, and against them the river reads up 504 cfs and 0.92 feet, which is where the rising flag comes from. The trace hour by hour: the crest was 2,100 cfs and 5.15 feet at 5:45 and 6 a.m. Thursday, then 2,000 at 7 a.m., 1,880 at 8, 1,740 at 9, 1,620 at 10, 1,540 at 11, 1,450 at noon, 1,370 at 1 p.m., 1,290 at 2, 1,250 at 3, 1,180 at 4, 1,160 at 5, 1,130 at 6, 1,100 at 7, 1,070 at 8, 1,060 at 9, 1,030 at 10, 1,020 at 11, 1,000 at midnight, 997 at 1 a.m., 976 at 2, 970 at 3, 963 at 4 and 950 cfs at 4:30, 5 and 5:15 a.m.; the hourly drops ran 100 to 140 cfs through the morning, 30 to 80 in the afternoon, 20 to 30 in the evening and under 10 overnight, so the recession has flattened in the 950-to-1,000 band for the last five hours. waters.working: Sixth day past the new moon: the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 26 percent lit and 5.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:48 a.m., puts the new moon at 15:50 UT Saturday, Oct. 10, the first quarter at 16:12 UT Sunday, Oct. 18, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26 and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so the spring tides are easing toward Sunday's neap: the surf's midday high has come down from 5.3 feet Monday, 5.0 Tuesday, 4.6 Wednesday and 5.0 Thursday to 4.7 today. NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender at 5:48 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no beach hazards statement, the fifth quiet beach morning in a row; what it did have, issued at 2:21 a.m. Friday for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles, the marine zone off the island and the inlet, is a Gale Warning for noon Saturday to 6 a.m. Monday, north winds 20 to 30 knots with gusts to 40 and seas 7 to 10 feet, which the Service says will capsize or damage vessels and cut visibility: a marine product, not a surf-zone one, and nothing in it for today. All four sound events fall inside Friday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.2 feet at 12:32 a.m., is at the bottom of its ebb at press time, a 0.9-foot low at 6:30 a.m., then fills 3.1 feet to a 4.0-foot high at 1:05 p.m. and drains 2.7 feet to a 1.3-foot low at 7:29 p.m., so the last two hours of the ebb, about 5:30 to 7:29 p.m., land in the early evening; the next sound high falls after midnight and belongs to Saturday's table. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 5:07 a.m. at 1.1, high 11:53 a.m. at 4.7, low 6:30 p.m. at 1.3 and high 12:13 a.m. Saturday at 3.4, printed with the fetcher's (Sat) tag so nobody reads it as tonight's, a 3.6- and 3.4-foot swing against Thursday's 4.1 and 3.9. Today's lags from the two tables are 72 minutes on the midday high and 83 and 59 minutes on the lows, with this morning's 12:32 a.m. sound high 69 minutes behind Thursday's 11:23 p.m. surf high from Thursday's file; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 77.2 degrees at 5:36 a.m., up 0.9 from Thursday's 76.3 and the warmest reading of the week for a second day. What is running is 15 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:48 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout early on topwater and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or artificials under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the sound is slack low at 6:30 a.m., dead water at first light, and the first moving water is the morning flood from about 7 a.m., mud minnows and shrimp the forage on the oyster bars and grass edges as they cover, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars on the early flood, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The 1:05 p.m. high puts 4.0 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 11 a.m. to 1:05 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the ebb, roughly 5:30 to 7:29 p.m., 48 minutes later than Thursday's and still a daylight start: finger mullet are the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low. On the evening flood after 7:29 p.m. the dock lights are the trout spot once the 26 percent crescent sets, though with Beaufort up again to 77.2 the cool-down the guides say the trout are waiting on has not come. Oysters are in their second day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side, with nothing on it today and 4.7 feet of water at the pier on the 11:53 a.m. high, is Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the morning flood and cut bait on the bottom for the slot reds in the evening, the pattern every pier in the report gives; from noon Saturday the Gale Warning's north wind and 7-to-10-foot seas are on that water through Monday morning. Slack at 6:30 a.m., 1:05 p.m. and 7:29 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
